chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Miskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man recited in the morning prayer the surah,
He عليه السلام said: There is no problem. And whoever begins with a surah, then it occurs to him to go back and recite another surah instead, there is no problem except
for he should not turn from it to another surah; and likewise,

key_terms.سُورَةٍ: a chapter of the Qur'an recited in salat (prayer)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, singled out here as an exception
key_terms.قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلْكَافِرُونَ: Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, likewise singled out as an exception
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: to go back or switch to another recitation

ai.seo_question: Can a person change to a different surah after starting one in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning changing the surah one is reciting in salat (prayer). It states that changing from one surah to another is generally permissible, except after beginning Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ and Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, from which one should not turn to another surah.
